study_design: Retrospective cohort study using participants in the 1970-1972 Nutrition Canada Survey with cancer follow-up through 31 December 1993.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Among the 3400 survey participants included in the study, 145 developed prostate cancer.
reason: The abstract evaluates subsequent development of prostate cancer overall but does not report an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incidence endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Subjects who drank more than 500 ml of tea per day experienced virtually the same risk as those who reported no tea consumption (rate ratio (RR) 1.02, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.62-1.65).
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate concerns overall prostate cancer incidence, with no aggressive disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Total alcohol consumption was not related to subsequent development of prostate cancer, although very moderate consumption of wine (< 10 g per day), relative to no consumption, showed an RR of 1.48 (95% CI 1.05-2.09).
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate concerns subsequent development of prostate cancer overall, not aggressive prostate cancer.
